title: Go SDK model-mapper, validators and streaming facade
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: Add a minimal, ergonomic layer to the Go SDK that 1) maps raw generation envelopes into strongly-typed model structs using a small set of generics helpers, 2) validates structured output contracts at decode time with pluggable validation rules, and 3) provides a streaming facade (async iterator-like) that exposes decoded items and surface-level backpressure controls for callers. This ticket focuses on API shape, reference implementation, and examples (not final perf tuning).
motivation: Customers implementing retrieval-augmented generation and multi-step parsing workflows need a safe, reusable way to consume streaming responses as typed objects. Current examples copy/repeat decode logic across repos and do ad-hoc error handling; we should provide a standard pattern in the Go SDK to reduce bugs and integration friction.
approach: Proposal: introduce package 'sdek' (structured decode) with three small primitives: Mapper[T any] (maps raw envelope -> T, returns decode error), Validator[T any] (runs rules on T, returns human-friendly errors), and StreamReader[T any] which wraps the existing stream decoder and yields either validated T or a structured error event. The StreamReader will expose a configurable buffer window and an optional soft-fail mode (skip invalid items and emit a warning). We'll implement a reference example: chat-parse -> Event struct with timestamp, author, content and an 'entities' list. Provide examples for both single-item streams and batched item streams.
acceptance_criteria: Public API documented in SDK reference (pkg godoc + short example)
Mapper + Validator generics implemented and unit tested with 90% coverage for decode paths
StreamReader provides backpressure param and demonstrates graceful handling of invalid items via soft-fail mode
Integration example added: ./examples/parse_events/main.go that connects to hosted API, streams, decodes to Event struct, validates, and prints metrics
One design doc + one implementation PR linking this ticket and passing CI

risks: Generics constraints may require small helper wrappers to avoid verbose call sites
Performance: additional allocations during decode may impact ultra-low-latency users; we should provide opt-out zero-copy path later
Compatibility: existing SDK users may prefer raw envelope consumption; default behavior must be opt-in
notes: Design trade-offs discussed in kickoff: keep API surface intentionally small, prefer composable validators over monolithic schema objects. We debated using reflection-based tag parsing vs explicit field tags; decided to ship explicit mappers + light helpers now and revisit reflection helpers if adoption shows need.
